title: The development and expansion of automated chest x-ray reading algorithms for childhood tuberculosis
text:
Tuberculosis (TB) is a leading cause of death in children, especially young children under 5 years and children
living with HIV. Greater access to chest X-ray is essential to improve timely diagnosis, and in this study, we will
develop and assess new artificial intelligence models that can help screen and diagnose childhood TB, and guide
the appropriate duration of treatment. If successful, these new digital tools could be integrated into clinical care
and public health efforts to reduce the burden of TB in children.

title: Novel Targeted Anticancer Agents from Marine Cyanobacteria
text:
Marine cyanobacteria produce selective anticancer agents with specific molecular targets. This research will
lead to the discovery and development of new compounds that could become new drug leads for the treatment
of drug-resistant cancers.

title: Neurobehavioral consequences of Mild Traumatic Brain Injury and addiction risk: a cotwin-control study
text:
Mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) is highly prevalent and can potentially have long-lasting consequences for
the brain, cognitive function, and behavior, including elevated risk for substance abuse and
psychopathology. In this study, we will use a powerful and rigorous cotwin control approach to identify causal
effects of TBI by comparing twins with mTBI history with their identical cotwins who never had a TBI. A better
understanding of long-lasting consequences of childhood and adolescent mTBI will promote the
development of more efficient treatment and rehabilitation efforts, as well as prevention of substance abuse
and psychopathology frequently associated with mTBI history.

title: Engineering Immunity for Broad Protection Against Betacoronaviruses
text:
Betacoronaviruses, including SARS-CoV-2, SARS-CoV and pre-emergent bat coronaviruses, pose a significant
threat to human health and broad countermeasures to prevent and treat these viruses are urgently needed. The
spike subunit 2 (S2) of betacoronaviruses is highly conserved, making it an attractive target for broadly acting
therapeutics. This proposal will generate new knowledge about the function of S2-directed antibodies and inform
novel approaches to vaccine development and antibody therapeutics for betacoronaviruses.

title: Resolving transcription factor target search mechanisms
text:
Transcription factors control gene expression by binding near target genes to regulate their expression.
How transcription factors find their target sites remains poorly understood, yet dysregulation of gene
expression is a major cause of disease. Here we propose to resolve this using a new microscope modality that
allows tracking of single transcription factors at extremely high spatiotemporal resolution.

title: Estradiol signaling pathways mediating sex differences in striatal synaptic plasticity
text: Female sex hormones contribute to sex differences in many aspects of substance use disorders, such as accelerated transition from casual use to addiction. Synaptic plasticity in dorsal striatal circuits is critical for reward learning and substance use behavior, and this plasticity is impaired by female sex hormones. Understanding how estradiol interacts with cocaine to modify mechanisms underlying synaptic plasticity in the dorsal striatum can illuminate mechanisms underlying sex differences in behavior and help to identify methods for improving treatments in females.

title: Enabling in vivo barcoded single-cell multiomics-compatible genome-wide screens in personalized tumor models using defined-copy somatic transgenesis
text:
CRISPR has revolutionized our approaches to study cancer, allowing rapid functional interrogation at
transcriptome-wide scales. However, single-cell sequencing compatible transcriptome-wide screens in
autochthonous genetically engineered models remain a challenge. Here we propose a novel methodology to
enable transcriptome-scale multiplex gain and loss of function CRISPR screens that is compatible with our
robust MADR tumor modeling approach in human 3D organoid models and well-characterized “off-the-shelf”
mouse lines.

title: Collaboration, Communication, and Coordination Center for ADSP (ADSP-4C)
text:
Since 2012, the Alzheimer’s Disease Sequencing Program (ADSP) has advanced understanding of
Alzheimer's Disease genetics and helped pave the way for better prevention, diagnosis, and treatment. The
new Collaboration, Communication, and Coordination Center for ADSP (ADSP-4C) will provide logistic and
scientific support to the ADSP in its next phase, to refocus and update ADSP organizational structure, enhance
broad collaborations with AD researchers, develop new internal and external communications and outreach,
and expand the pool of engaged scientists through targeted education and training initiatives.

title: Conjugate nanoparticle platform development for HIV-1 envelope immunogens
text:
A protective HIV-1 vaccine is needed to halt the spread of the pandemic. This Program will move into
manufacturing a rapid vaccine platform that presents multiple copies of neutralizing antibody targets to the
immune system. This vaccine platform will hasten progress towards finding a protective HIV-1 vaccine.

title: Novel diagnostic algorithms to improve antimicrobial management for Ugandan patients with chemotherapy-associated febrile illness
text:
Chemotherapy-associated febrile illness is a major complication of cancer treatment and is associated with
high morbidity and mortality, particularly for patients living in sub-Saharan Africa. The cause of fever in many
cases is unknown, especially in places where the burden of HIV infection is high. For this project, we will
evaluate the causes of fever among people with chemotherapy-associated febrile illness in an HIV and TB
endemic setting.

title: Malaria parasite determinants of host cell tropism
text:
Malaria is caused by infection of red blood cells (RBCs) with Plasmodium parasites and can result in severe or
even fatal disease. Parasite polymorphisms that allow parasites to proliferate or persist in specific cell types
present a major challenge to malaria disease control and elimination, respectively. Here, we propose to elucidate
the molecular basis of two particular parasitic features that are of great public health importance, both for
designing appropriate interventions and for anticipating the emergence of new strains into the population: the
preference of P. falciparum for the youngest of human RBCs known as reticulocytes, and the adaptation of P.
falciparum to human RBCs from gorilla cells.

title: Unraveling the Mechanisms of Opioid-Induced Airway Constriction: A Path towards Novel Therapeutics for Opioid Overdose
text:
This project aims to investigate the neural mechanisms of fentanyl-induced respiratory depression, specifically
focusing on airway constriction and rhythmic disruptions. The project proposes the development of dual-action
treatments that address these issues without reversing the opioid's effect, offering a new approach to combating
opioid overdoses. Using a combination of cutting-edge techniques like in-vitro and in-vivo electrophysiology,
optogenetics, high-density neuronal network analysis, and viral-based manipulation, we aspire to provide
significant breakthroughs in our understanding and treatment of opioid-induced respiratory depression.

title: Modeling breast cancer through a developmental lens of mammary lineage commitment
text:
Advances in sequencing technologies to profile large number of human breast tumors has identified several
oncofetal genes that are mutated at a low frequency, which impose significant challenges in detection and
diagnosis. These genes, essential during embryonic development, are reactivated in tumor development,
correlating with poor prognosis in breast cancers. This project aims to identify and characterize these embryonic
mammary lineage genes, offering potential candidates for improved diagnosis, prognosis, and therapeutic
strategies.

title: Integrated Microscopy Core Facility
text: The enhanced capabilities of the IMCore will advance fundamental research on sensory and nervous system function, directly contributing to our understanding of neurological disorders including chronic pain, epilepsy, and sensory processing conditions. These developments will support the development of future therapeutic strategies to improve patient outcomes.

title: Translational Imaging Research Program in Radiopharmaceutical Sciences
text:
Project Narrative.
The Washington University T32 postdoctoral training grant “Translational Imaging in
Radiopharmaceutical Sciences” (abbreviated as “TIRS”) is a multidisciplinary initiative to train the
next generation of PET molecular imaging scientists to design, develop, and translate diagnostic
agents for imaging of neurodegenerative diseases and ADRDs. To accomplish this novel
training mission, the T32 TIRS program brings leading scientists from 12 departments of
Washington University on a single platform to provide proposed multidisciplinary training.
Successful accomplishment of training goals (as outlined in program plan) will deliver molecular
PET imaging research scientists who would be transitioning into faculty positions nationwide and
will be expected to serve the field of diagnostic nuclear medicine in neuroscience for several
decades.

title: Leveraging mouse models and retinal organoids to optimize a gene therapy for IMPG2-associated retinal degeneration
text:
Mutations in a gene known as IMPG2 lead to various forms of severe visual impairment. A potential treatment
involves packaging the IMPG2 gene into adeno-associated virus (AAV) particles that are used to deliver the
gene to photoreceptors. Here we will leverage our recent development of mouse models and human retinal
organoids to engineer a gene therapy to treat IMPG2-linked forms of retinal degeneration, with the expectation
that our synergistic use of these dual models will also provide a general approach to rapidly advance safe and
effective therapeutics for other inherited retinal disorders.

title: Flexible Bayesian methods for zero-inflated microbiome data to understand microbial community dynamics and function
text:
The integration of microbiota-based strategies into personalized medicine has immense potential for improving
patient outcomes. However, a major challenge in advancing microbiota-based personalized medicine is our limited
understanding of the mechanisms driving microbial community assembly, stability, and function, compounded by
limitations of existing statistical and machine learning methods. To fill this gap, we will develop a suite of scalable
Bayesian statistical methods and accompanying software packages to help researchers better understand these
mechanisms while properly accommodating the high-dimensional, overdispersed, zero-inflated, and compositional
structure characteristic of microbiome data.

title: Biostatistics and Computational Biology (BCB) Core
text:
CORE 2_ BIOSTATISTICS AND COMPUTATIONAL BIOLOGY: NARRATIVE
The Biostatistics and Computational Biology (BCB) Core for this P01 will enable cost-effective data processing,
analysis, and contextualization of the omics data generated for all Projects and ensure rapid dissemination and
easy access of these data.

title: Age-related repetitive element dysregulation, neuroinflammation and Alzheimer's disease
text:
Alzheimer’s disease is associated with an accumulation of repetitive RNAs that may play a role in development
of the disease. The purpose of this research project is to determine if repetitive RNA accumulation in
Alzheimer’s disease can be explained by age-related increases in these RNAs, and to determine if they
contribute to the inflammation observed in both contexts. This work may help us understand how and why
aging increases the risk for Alzheimer’s disease, and it could provide insight on potential therapeutic strategies
for inhibiting these events.

title: Precision UCART and Nanoparticle Combination to Combat Hostile Microenvironments (PUNCH)
text:
Metastatic pancreatic cancer resists existing therapies and often progresses too rapidly for patients to be
treated with autologous CART cell therapy, This project develops a novel, off-the-shelf CART cell therapy
combined with a tumor-targeted lipid nanoparticle system that delivers therapeutic mRNAs and a
conjugated immune checkpoint inhibitor, designed to overcome tumor-intrinsic and adaptive resistance
mechanisms, Together, these components form a synergistic immunotherapy platform with the potential to
transform outcomes for patients with metastatic pancreatic cancer.
